title: NavigationTransition
description: A directed edge between exactly one source Route and one destination Route that records a single permitted route change in the client-side router, together with the mechanism that initiates it (user click, programmatic call, timeout, browser history, or redirect). It represents the move between routes, not either route, and carries no sequence position in a multi-step process. Use Route instead when the element is the addressable URL pattern or route-table entry itself, including a route declared with type 'redirect' or 'alias', rather than the move from one route to another. Use FlowStep instead when the element is an ordered position in a multi-step process (it has a sequence index and a required/wait behavior) rather than an edge between two routes. Use GuardAction instead when the redirect or block is the response a NavigationGuard executes on denial, with a message and preserveRoute setting, rather than a modeled edge between two routes. Use RouteMeta instead when 'transition' refers to the CSS or animation effect applied on entering or leaving a route (e.g. 'fade'), not to a route-to-route edge.

from.description: Identifier (Route ID or path pattern) of the source Route from which the transition starts; set to the route whose view or config contains the link, call, or redirect, or to '*' only when the transition can be fired from any route.

to.description: Identifier (Route ID or path pattern, with parameter placeholders such as '/orders/:id') of the destination Route that becomes active once the transition completes; always set to a Route defined in the same NavigationGraph.

trigger.description: Mechanism that initiates the route transition: user-click (explicit user interaction), programmatic (code-driven), timeout (time-based), browser-back (browser history navigation), redirect (automatic server/guard redirect).

description.description: Free-text explanation of when and why the transition occurs, such as the UI control or business event that fires it; set when the trigger alone does not make the user intent clear.

x-dr-standard: SPA Navigation Patterns: declarative and programmatic navigation (route change via History API pushState/replaceState/popstate)
x-dr-evidence: A router link component (<Link to="/orders">, <router-link :to="{name:'checkout'}">, [routerLink]) rendered in the view of one route and targeting another route

An imperative navigation call such as router.push(), navigate('/x'), history.replace(), Navigator.pushNamed() or this.router.navigateByUrl() inside an event handler, effect, form-submit callback, or setTimeout
A route-table entry or loader/guard return that forwards one path to another, e.g. { path: '/old', redirect: '/new' }, <Navigate to="/login" replace/>, or return redirect('/dashboard')
